title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche notes, c. 1981, section-conjecture material). K is a field of finite type (presumably over Q, so characteristic 0), L/K is a function field, and E_L^{\bar L} = Gal(\bar L/L) is viewed as an extension of E_K = Gal(\bar K/K). U is an 'elementary' model of L/K, and E_U^{\bar L} = π_1(U) is the arithmetic fundamental group, with geometric part π_{U/K}^{\bar L} = π_1(U_{\bar K}). Conjecture b) on the previous page relates Galois sections of E_L → E_K to sections of E_U → E_K. Valuation rings V of L/K (trivial on K) give sections through their decomposition groups N_V, which contain the inertia \bar I_V. Conjecture (32) asserts (E_L^{\bar L})^{Γ^0} = 1; (33) gives the version for π_{L/K}. The first lines here say this generalises the analogous conjecture already made in relative dimension 1, i.e. for curves.

Programme on this page. To understand part b), Grothendieck proposes two steps.
(i) Push the V-sections of E_L → E_K forward along E_L → E_U.
(ii) Study Δ_V := Im(\bar I_V → π_{U/K}^{\bar L}), the image of the inertia group of V in the geometric fundamental group of U. He expects Δ_V to play the role of a 'groupe-lacet', i.e. an analogue of the cusp inertia (loop around a puncture) for curves.
He then asks to what extent distinct V give distinct Δ_V.

Tool. Choose a proper model X ⊃ U of L/K such that D = X − U is a normal crossings divisor with regular components D_i (i ∈ I). For x ∈ Supp D, take the henselisation Õ_x of O_{X,x} and Ũ_x = U ×_X Spec Õ_x, the 'punctured tubular neighbourhood'.

Next page. Abhyankar's lemma / Grothendieck–Murre gives (34): 1 → \hat Z(1)^{I(x)} → π_1(Ũ_x) → Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)) → 1, with I(x) = {i : x ∈ D_i}. If V has centre x on Supp D, then N_V → E_U factors through N_x := Im(π_1(Ũ_x) → π_1(U)), the decomposition group of x.

Modern reading. In characteristic 0, \bar I_V ≅ Hom(Γ_V, \hat Z(1)), where Γ_V is the value group. This maps into the local monodromy torus \hat Z(1)^{I(x)} by the transpose of Z^{I(x)} → Γ_V, e_i ↦ v(t_i), where t_i is a local equation of D_i. So Δ_V is a subgroup of the image of the local boundary inertia at the centre x. It is determined by the 'monomial data' (v(t_i)) of V at x, and by its position in the conjugacy class.
errors: Henselisation ambiguity: 'point strict' together with 'hensélisé' is unclear. Exact sequence (34), with quotient Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)), requires the ordinary henselisation at a scheme point. Over a strict henselisation that quotient would be trivial.

The question 'do distinct V give distinct Δ_V' cannot have a positive answer in general. Every V whose centre lies in U has Δ_V = 1. Valuations centred on D with proportional monomial data (v(t_i)) give the same Δ_V up to conjugacy. So Δ_V alone can separate at most the 'boundary type' of V; finer separation must use N_V or its image N_x. The text poses this as an open question, not as a wrong claim.

ideas.what: Image Δ_V of the inertia group of a valuation of L/K in the geometric fundamental group of an open model U, viewed as a higher-dimensional analogue of cusp/loop inertia
ideas.modern_name: boundary inertia subgroups of π_1 of a higher-dimensional variety; images of inertia of (divisorial or Abhyankar) valuations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Curves: cusp inertia studied by Nakamura, Mochizuki, Tamagawa. Higher dimension and valuation-theoretic: Pop, Bogomolov–Tschinkel, Stix, Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: The Longue Marche notes are only partly published/circulated (transcriptions by Lochak et al. and the Montpellier archive); not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: Local π_1 of the complement of a normal crossings divisor in a henselian local scheme as an extension of the residue Galois group by \hat Z(1)^{I(x)}
ideas.modern_name: Abhyankar's lemma / tame local fundamental group (Grothendieck–Murre)

ideas.what: Relating sections of Gal(L) → Gal(K) coming from valuations to sections of π_1(U) → Gal(K) via decomposition groups of centres on a normal crossings compactification
ideas.modern_name: birational vs. ordinary section conjecture; valuation-theoretic sections and packets at infinity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1983 letter to Faltings); developed by Koenigsmann, Pop, Stix, Esnault–Wittenberg
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) states the section conjecture, but not this higher-dimensional valuation analysis

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses the question of to what extent distinct valuations V of L/K give distinct inertia images Δ_V in π_1(U_{\bar K}), with Δ_V treated as a 'loop group'. This is a higher-dimensional generalisation of 'distinct cusps have distinct, non-conjugate inertia groups' for hyperbolic curves. The thread is left open on this page.
missed.quote: étudier le Δ_V sous-groupe de π^{\bar L}_{U/K} image de \bar I_V — qui, on le devine, jouera un rôle analogue à un groupe-lacet. Dans quelle mesure des V distinctes définissent-elles des Δ_V distinctes ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recovering boundary data (which strata, which monomial valuations) from the group-theoretic images of inertia in π_1 of higher-dimensional varieties is still only partly developed beyond curves and configuration spaces. The question is related to, but not identical with, Pop's recovery of valuations from the birational Galois group. Its answer is negative for Δ_V alone, so the information must sit in N_V or N_x.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic setup: it reduces to local tame fundamental groups at a normal crossings compactification, which is standard. The one non-routine element is the 'loop group' viewpoint on images of valuation inertia in higher dimension and the separation question. That is a natural extension of known curve-case results and is broadly in line with later anabelian work, so it is not a hidden theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'Pour mieux appréhender cette dimension[?] particulière b)' should probably read 'cette direction particulière b)'.
Fragment 'il faudrait examiner de plus près ce que deviennent' is confirmed; 'sections de E^{\bar L}_L sur E_K associées à une V' matches the image.
'(point strict)' is a superscript insertion above 'considérons le hensélisé', not part of the main line. It qualifies x and leaves the strict-vs-ordinary henselisation ambiguous.
Inserted labels: 'D_i (i∈I)' is written above 'comp. irréd.', and 'D=' above 'X−U'.
